title: Concrete Methods in Abstract Classes
summary: Learn how combining concrete and abstract methods provides partial abstraction, enables code reuse, and powers the Template Method design pattern.
learningObjectives: Design abstract classes that balance shared concrete utility logic with abstract customization hooks
Implement the Template Method design pattern using final concrete workflow methods
Identify when to provide default concrete implementations that subclasses can optionally override
Trace dynamic dispatch when an inherited concrete method invokes an abstract method
expectedOutcomes: You can build structured processing pipelines using concrete orchestration methods
You understand how partial abstraction eliminates boilerplate code across sibling subclasses

activities.title: Everyday Analogy: The Automated Car Wash

realWorldMetaphor.scenario: An automated drive-through car wash has a rigid standard procedure: 1. Soak vehicle, 2. Apply cleaning formula, 3. Rinse with pressurized water, 4. Blow dry with high-velocity air. Steps 1, 3, and 4 are identical for every car (concrete). Step 2 is customized depending on whether the customer chose Basic Soap, Hot Carnauba Wax, or Ceramic Shield (abstract).
realWorldMetaphor.mapping: The overarching workflow (`washCar()`) is a concrete method in the abstract base class. Steps 1, 3, and 4 are concrete methods. Step 2 (`applyChemicals()`) is an abstract method delegated to concrete tier subclasses.
realWorldMetaphor.takeaway: An abstract class can lock down the overall algorithmic flow with concrete methods while delegating specific variant steps to abstract methods.

activities.explanation: A hook method is a concrete method providing an empty or boolean default. Subclasses can override it to conditionally alter the algorithm flow without modifying the template.

activities.title: Concrete Methods in Abstract Classes Quiz

questions.question: What is the primary architectural purpose of defining concrete methods inside an abstract class?
options: To allow the abstract class to be instantiated with new
To share common, reusable code across all subclasses, preventing code duplication
To make all methods in the class static
To bypass method overriding rules
questions.explanation: Concrete methods in an abstract class encapsulate common functionality once, ensuring all extending subclasses inherit and reuse that logic without rewriting it.

questions.question: In the Template Method pattern, why is the main orchestration method typically declared `final`?
options: To make it run faster in multithreaded environments
To prevent subclasses from altering the high-level sequence and invariants of the algorithm
Because non-final methods cannot call abstract methods
To prevent the method from using instance fields
questions.explanation: Marking the template method `final` enforces that subclasses cannot override or reorder the algorithm steps, preserving business invariants.

questions.question: What is a 'hook method' in an abstract class?
options: A native method written in C
A concrete method with an empty or default implementation that subclasses can optionally override to control behavior
A method that intercepts garbage collection
An abstract method with no parameters
questions.explanation: A hook method is a concrete method that provides a default no-op or boolean flag, allowing subclasses to hook into the template algorithm optionally.

questions.question: Can a concrete method in an abstract superclass be overridden by a subclass?
options: No, only abstract methods can be overridden
Yes, unless the concrete method is declared final or private
Only if marked with @Overridable
Only if the subclass is also abstract
questions.explanation: Any non-final, non-private concrete method in an abstract class can be freely overridden by subclasses to customize or replace behavior.

questions.question: When a concrete method in an abstract class calls an abstract method in the same class, what happens?
options: Compilation error: cannot call unimplemented method
The JVM uses dynamic method dispatch to call the subclass's overridden implementation
An AbstractMethodError is always thrown
The program exits
questions.explanation: The call is dispatched dynamically via the runtime object's vtable, executing the concrete child's implementation.

questions.question: What percentage of abstraction is provided by an abstract class in Java?
options: Strictly 100%
Strictly 0%
Partial abstraction (anywhere from 0% to 100%)
Strictly 50%
questions.explanation: Abstract classes provide partial abstraction: they can have 0% abstract methods (all concrete), 100% abstract methods, or any mix in between.

questions.question: Can a concrete method in an abstract class access `private` fields of that abstract class?
options: No, abstract classes cannot have private fields
Yes, concrete methods have full access to private fields declared within their own class
Only through getters
Only if the fields are static
questions.explanation: A concrete method belongs to the declaring class and therefore has full access to all private members declared in that class.

questions.question: What is the difference between an abstract method and a concrete hook method?
options: Abstract methods MUST be implemented by concrete subclasses; hook methods are optional to override
Hook methods cannot return values
Abstract methods must be static
There is no difference
questions.explanation: Abstract methods force subclasses to provide an implementation; concrete hook methods provide a default body that subclasses may choose to override or ignore.

questions.question: If an abstract class has 5 concrete methods and 1 abstract method, how many methods MUST a concrete subclass implement?
options: All 6 methods
Only the 1 abstract method
At least 3 methods
None of them
questions.explanation: The concrete subclass is only obligated to implement the 1 abstract method. It inherits the 5 concrete methods automatically.

questions.question: How does the 'Hollywood Principle' ('Don't call us, we'll call you') relate to concrete methods in abstract classes?
options: Classes can only be created by movie actors
High-level concrete template methods control the workflow and call low-level subclass abstract methods when needed
Constructors cannot call super()
Subclasses must call System.exit()
questions.explanation: The Hollywood Principle describes the inversion of control in template methods: the parent workflow calls down into subclass overrides rather than child code calling parent steps manually.

activities.title: Interview Questions: Concrete Methods in Abstract Classes

interviewQA.question: What is the Template Method design pattern, and how does it leverage concrete and abstract methods?
interviewQA.answer: The Template Method pattern defines the algorithmic skeleton in a concrete superclass method (often declared `final` to protect integrity). That template method coordinates execution by invoking private helper methods for invariant steps, protected abstract methods for mandatory specialized steps, and concrete hook methods for optional customizations. Concrete subclasses supply the custom steps without altering the master workflow.

interviewQA.question: When would you prefer an abstract class with concrete methods over a Java 8 interface with default methods?
interviewQA.answer: Prefer an abstract class when: 1. You need instance state (non-static, non-final fields like `balance` or `userSession`), 2. You need constructors to enforce state invariants, 3. You need non-public access modifiers (`protected` or package-private helper methods), or 4. You are modeling an 'IS-A' identity hierarchy rather than a 'CAN-DO' behavioral capability.

interviewQA.question: What is a 'hook' method in an abstract base class, and why is it useful?
interviewQA.answer: A hook is a concrete method in an abstract class that has an empty body or returns a default boolean flag (e.g. `protected boolean isAuditEnabled() { return false; }`). It gives subclasses the option to hook into the workflow at defined interception points without making implementation mandatory like an abstract method.

interviewQA.question: What is the risk of making template methods non-final?
interviewQA.answer: If a template method is non-final, a subclass can override it completely, discarding the orchestration logic, skipping mandatory security checks or auditing steps, and breaking system invariants.

interviewQA.question: Can a concrete method in an abstract class be declared `static`? What are its limitations?
interviewQA.answer: Yes. An abstract class can have static concrete methods (e.g. factory methods or math helpers). However, a static method cannot invoke abstract instance methods or access instance variables without an explicit object reference, because static methods execute without a `this` context.

interviewQA.question: How does partial abstraction help adhere to the DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principle?
interviewQA.answer: In complex domain models with many sibling subclasses (e.g. 10 types of database connectors), 80% of the lifecycle (connection timeout handling, retry backoff, metric publishing) is identical. By placing that 80% in concrete methods within an abstract base class, you eliminate duplicated code across all 10 subclasses.

activities.title: Self-Evaluation Checklist
checklist: I understand why abstract classes provide partial abstraction (0% to 100%).
I can implement the Template Method pattern using a final concrete orchestration method.
I understand how the Hollywood Principle ('Don't call us, we'll call you') applies to abstract workflows.
I know why making template methods `final` prevents subclasses from violating invariants.
I understand how hook methods provide optional extension points for subclasses.
I know that concrete methods in abstract classes can access private fields and constructors.
I know that subclasses are only required to implement abstract methods, inheriting concrete ones.
I can contrast abstract classes with default methods in interfaces regarding state and visibility.
I understand how dynamic method dispatch resolves abstract method calls made from concrete parent methods.
I can design an end-to-end data processing pipeline combining concrete and abstract steps.

practiceProblems.title: Warmup: Beverage Maker Template Method
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Complete the `BeverageMaker` template method hierarchy:
1. Abstract class `BeverageMaker`: has template method `public final void makeBeverage()` calling `boilWater()`, `brew()`, `pourInCup()`, and `addCondiments()`.
   - `boilWater()` is concrete: prints `'Boiling water'`.
   - `pourInCup()` is concrete: prints `'Pouring into cup'`.
   - `brew()` is abstract.
   - `addCondiments()` is abstract.
2. Concrete class `TeaMaker` extending `BeverageMaker`:
   - Overrides `brew()` printing `'Steeping the tea bags'`.
   - Overrides `addCondiments()` printing `'Adding lemon slices'`.
In `main`, instantiate a `TeaMaker` referenced as `BeverageMaker` and call `makeBeverage()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Boiling water
Steeping the tea bags
Pouring into cup
Adding lemon slices
hints: In BeverageMaker, add public abstract void brew(); and public abstract void addCondiments();

practiceProblems.title: Data Pipeline with Optional Compression Hook
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a data ingestion pipeline from scratch using a template method and hook:
1. Abstract class `DataIngestionPipeline`: has template method `public final void runPipeline(String source)` which:
   - Calls `readSource(source)` (concrete method printing `'[Read] Ingesting ' + source`).
   - If `shouldCompress()` (hook method returning `false` by default) is true, calls `compress()` (concrete method printing `'[Compress] Applying GZIP compression'`).
   - Calls `saveData()` (abstract method).
2. Concrete class `StandardIngestion` extending `DataIngestionPipeline`:
   - Overrides `saveData()` printing `'[Save] Writing raw records to warehouse'`.
3. Concrete class `ArchivalIngestion` extending `DataIngestionPipeline`:
   - Overrides `shouldCompress()` returning `true`.
   - Overrides `saveData()` printing `'[Save] Archiving compressed payload to cold storage'`.
4. In `Main`, run `ArchivalIngestion` on source `'sensor_logs.csv'`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
[Read] Ingesting sensor_logs.csv
[Compress] Applying GZIP compression
[Save] Archiving compressed payload to cold storage
hints: ArchivalIngestion overrides shouldCompress() to return true, activating compress().

practiceProblems.title: Abstract Game AI Turn Execution
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a turn-based game AI pipeline from scratch:
1. Abstract class `GameCharacter`: has `protected String name` and `protected int health = 100`.
   Constructor sets `name`.
   Concrete method `public void takeDamage(int amt)`: subtracts amt from health and prints `name + ' takes ' + amt + ' damage (Health: ' + health + ')'`.
   Template method `public final void takeTurn()`: prints `'--- ' + name + "'s Turn ---"`, calls `chooseAction()`, calls `postTurnCleanup()`.
   Abstract method `protected abstract void chooseAction()`.
   Concrete hook method `protected void postTurnCleanup()`: prints `name + ' finishes turn safely'`.
2. Concrete class `Warrior` extending `GameCharacter`:
   - Overrides `chooseAction()` printing `name + ' swings broadsword for heavy strike!'`.
3. Concrete class `Wizard` extending `GameCharacter`:
   - Overrides `chooseAction()` printing `name + ' casts Arcane Shield!'`.
   - Overrides `postTurnCleanup()` printing `name + ' regenerates 5 mana points'`.
4. In `Main`, create an array with a `Warrior("Conan")` and a `Wizard("Gandalf")`. Call `takeTurn()` on each.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
--- Conan's Turn ---
Conan swings broadsword for heavy strike!
Conan finishes turn safely
--- Gandalf's Turn ---
Gandalf casts Arcane Shield!
Gandalf regenerates 5 mana points
hints: Wizard overrides both chooseAction() and postTurnCleanup().
Warrior only overrides chooseAction() and inherits the default postTurnCleanup().

practiceProblems.title: Bug Hunt: Broken Subclass Template Override
practiceProblems.problemStatement: A developer forgot to make the template method `processPayment()` final, allowing a subclass to accidentally override and destroy the mandatory audit logging step. Fix the class architecture so `processPayment()` is sealed with `final` and the subclass only overrides the abstract step.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
[AUDIT] Starting payment for $50.0
QuickPay network transfer executed: $50.0
[AUDIT] Payment successfully cleared
hints: Add final to public final void processPayment(double amount).
Delete the overridden processPayment method in QuickPay so it only implements executeTransaction(amount).

practiceProblems.title: Abstract ETL Workflow Engine
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build an Extract-Transform-Load (ETL) processing engine from scratch:
1. Abstract class `EtlJob`: has `protected String datasetName`. Constructor initializes `datasetName`.
   Template method `public final void execute()`:
   - Calls `extract()` (abstract: returns String rawData).
   - Calls `transform(rawData)` (abstract: accepts String rawData, returns String cleanData).
   - If `validate(cleanData)` (concrete hook: returns `cleanData != null && !cleanData.isEmpty()`), calls `load(cleanData)` (abstract).
   - Else prints `'Validation failed for ' + datasetName`.
2. Concrete class `CustomerEtlJob` extending `EtlJob`:
   - Constructor accepts `String datasetName` and passes to `super(datasetName)`.
   - `extract()` returns `'raw_cust_101,john doe'`.
   - `transform(rawData)` returns `rawData.toUpperCase().replace("RAW_", "CLEAN_")`.
   - `load(cleanData)` prints `'Loaded into Customer Data Warehouse: ' + cleanData`.
3. In `Main`, create a `CustomerEtlJob("Q3_Customers")` and call `execute()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput: Loaded into Customer Data Warehouse: CLEAN_CUST_101,JOHN DOE
hints: In CustomerEtlJob.transform, convert rawData to uppercase and replace RAW_ with CLEAN_.
execute() coordinates the entire ETL pipeline.
